lab_binary.kind: O1 JOIN-override unchanged defaults, glibc laboratory build

fixture.name: Small, synthetic, time-relative RecentSamples TTL fixture

math_bound: Recent samples selection requires oldest requested sample time >= now-TTL+60s. Main samples is required for cold/straddling queries. With duplicated hot rows, bytes_on_disk(main)+bytes_on_disk(recent) >= bytes_on_disk(main), but fixed small-part headers dominate; do not extrapolate bytes/sample.
method: One clean isolated ubuntu-24.04 native TimeSeries server. Same data, source, binary, native avg by(case_id)(avg_over_time(metric[window])) with RecentSamples preference 0 and 1. Six windows per each of initial, late/out-of-order insert and after OPTIMIZE FINAL. Exact label/time and mean-value equivalence against independent Python oracle, and physical EXPLAIN PLAN sample-table choice.

measurements.note: Correctness-only test; observed small-part bytes are not a steady-state write cost or per-sample storage ratio

limitations: Time-relative fixture executed only once on an isolated runner; no TTL actually elapsed during test, so this is route-safety not physical TTL-delete validation.
No native query latency, CPU, RSS, ingestion throughput, p95 or merge CPU comparison.
No crash-recovery, simultaneous read+write, multi-node or readonly/ACL cases.
Only O1 laboratory ClickHouse without jemalloc; no production performance claim.
stop_condition: Do not promote RecentSamples as a performance improvement until production allocator, duplicate writes/merges, TTL expiration and native p95 CPU/RSS are measured.

next_action.step: Use the existing root R04 claim and its evidence. Design separate measured steady-state hot TTL read-write factorial with exact same query input/binary, including physical expiration and restart; do not create a duplicate root claim or CI job while other agents own R01/R03.
next_action.stop_condition: Reject if native parity fails, post-expiry data mismatch, write amplification exceeds budget, or full broad query reaches memory cap.
